source_caption:
🎬 Toast (2010)

Toast follows Nigel Slater, a young boy growing up in 1960s England who discovers a passion for cooking while navigating a complicated family life. Raised by a loving mother who struggles in the kitchen and a strict father who finds it difficult to express his emotions, Nigel begins finding comfort and happiness through food. After a heartbreaking family loss, his life changes when his father develops a relationship with Mrs. Potter, a talented cook whose delicious meals spark an unexpected rivalry. Determined to prove himself, Nigel begins experimenting with recipes and developing the culinary skills that will eventually shape his future. Starring Freddie Highmore, Helena Bonham Carter, and Ken Stott, the film combines heartfelt drama, gentle humor, and nostalgic moments while exploring family, grief, ambition, and the comforting power of food.

🎭 Genre: Biography • Comedy • Drama

⭐ IMDb: 6.6/10

⏱️ Runtime: 1h 36m • TV-PG

🎥 Director: S. J. Clarkson

✍️ Writer: Lee Hall

📚 Based On: Toast: The Story of a Boy’s Hunger by Nigel Slater

source_details.synopsis: Toast is a 2010 British biographical comedy-drama film based on the autobiographical novel of the same name by the cookery writer Nigel Slater. The film was directed by S. J. Clarkson and written by Lee Hall. The cast includes Freddie Highmore, Helena Bonham Carter, Ken Stott and Oscar Kennedy. It received a gala at the 2011 Berlin International Film Festival. As a television film it was first broadcast on BBC One on 30 December 2010 and was given a theatrical release in cinemas on 11 August 2011. In 2018, it was adapted for stage by Henry Filloux-Bennett. It first premiered at Week 53 Festival in March with a subsequent run at the Edinburgh Festival Fringe. In April 2019, it opened in Londo
